issues.legal_issue: A court may enforce its eviction order by directing delivery of possession when the party granted time on an assurance of filing an undertaking fails to deliver possession and related persons act to frustrate the order.
material_facts: An eviction order against the firm was upheld, and the Supreme Court deferred its execution for six months after the firm represented that it would file the usual undertaking.
The firm did not file an undertaking and did not deliver vacant possession.
Sons of the firm's partners later brought a suit claiming an independent tenancy right and obtained an injunction that impeded delivery of possession.
The Court found that the conduct of the firm and the related persons was calculated to frustrate its order and that the applicants were entitled to have the eviction order executed.
issues.conclusion: The Court directed the trial court to cause vacant possession to be delivered, with police assistance if necessary, and to report compliance.
issues.legal_principle: An order of the Court must be implemented and cannot be defeated by conduct designed to frustrate it. Although Babu Ram Gupta v. Sudhir Bhasin holds that breach of an undertaking requires an express undertaking and that an implied undertaking cannot be assumed, the Court distinguished that rule from its power in this case to ensure compliance with its order. Thackar Hariram Motiram v. Balkrishan Chatrathu Thacker was also cited in connection with time granted in an eviction matter.

rule.if: post_eviction_order_enforcement_proceeding and court_granted_time_on_assurance_of_undertaking and undertaking_not_filed and possession_not_delivered and related_persons_obstructed_execution

predicates.post_eviction_order_enforcement_proceedi: An application is made to secure enforcement of a court's eviction order.
predicates.court_granted_time_on_assurance_of_under: The court deferred execution after the party seeking time represented that it would file an undertaking to deliver possession.
predicates.undertaking_not_filed: The party that obtained time did not file the promised undertaking.
predicates.possession_not_delivered: Vacant possession was not delivered as required by the court's order.
predicates.related_persons_obstructed_execution: Persons connected with the party whose eviction was ordered took steps that impeded execution of the order.

issues.definition: When an eviction-order enforcement proceeding involves an unfulfilled assurance, undelivered possession, and obstruction by related persons, the rule permits the court to direct delivery of possession.

issues.legal_issue: Failure to deliver possession cannot be treated as breach of an undertaking for contempt when no undertaking was given.
material_facts: The firm obtained time to vacate after representing that it would file the usual undertaking.
No undertaking, written or otherwise, was given to the Court.
The applicants sought contempt proceedings based on the failure to deliver possession.
issues.conclusion: The firm could not be found guilty of violating an undertaking because no undertaking had been given, though the Court separately ensured compliance with its order.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 2(b) of the Contempt of Courts Act, 1971, as explained in Babu Ram Gupta v. Sudhir Bhasin, wilful breach of an undertaking may constitute contempt where the undertaking is expressly given, in writing or orally and recorded by the court; a court cannot assume an implied undertaking where none is on the record.

predicates.contempt_proceeding: An application seeks to hold a person in contempt for failure to comply with a court-related obligation.
predicates.undertaking_not_given: The person did not expressly give an undertaking to the court, whether in writing or orally.

issues.definition: In a contempt proceeding, where no express undertaking was given, the failure cannot be treated as contempt by breach of undertaking.

issues.legal_issue: The one-year limitation for initiating contempt proceedings does not bar an application concerning a continuing failure to deliver possession when the application is made within one year of the relevant obstructive act.
material_facts: The applicants filed their application on or about 3 November 1988.
The alleged contempt included continued non-delivery of possession and conduct connected with an injunction order made on 12 February 1988.
The Court treated the failure to give possession in the circumstances as a continuing wrong.
issues.conclusion: The application was within one year and the continuing failure to deliver possession left no scope for applying the statutory limitation bar.
issues.legal_principle: Section 20 of the Contempt of Courts Act, 1971 bars initiation of contempt proceedings after one year from the date of the alleged contempt; the Court held that failure to give possession in this situation was a continuing wrong and also noted that the application was filed within one year of the relevant act.

predicates.contempt_proceeding: An application seeks initiation of proceedings for contempt of court.
predicates.continuing_failure_to_deliver_possession: The failure to deliver possession persists rather than being confined to a completed past act.
predicates.application_within_one_year: The contempt application is made within one year of the relevant alleged obstructive act.

issues.definition: When a contempt application concerns a continuing failure to deliver possession and is made within one year of the relevant act, the limitation bar does not apply.
